items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Mahler, he had the regular German folk tradition, and the Jewish folk tradition in there. You could take certain parts of Mahler songs and you could turn them into klezmer tunes in two seconds.

ctx.x: Yeah, too a greater, or lesser extent.

They all did. [You know…] It comes out of the folk music. It’s not detached from …. Well, twentieth-century music, a lot of that is detached from the people. But, before that, whether you’re talking about Bach, or Mozart, all this music Bach has this … he did an entire rearrangement of old traditional Christian songs. They are finding all this stuff that he did. Songs by other people that he just reharmonized and added …and they have. I have the record right now. There is so much folk music in Mozart’s music.…
Shoot, Mahler was checking out Chinese.
